_about: W-O-O-F News, the open line bank (docs/handoff-2026-10-22.md §4 and §7b, and the Claude Doc 'W-O-O-F News Recording Script'). Every line is written and Jon may see them all; only which one plays is the case's. Each line's clip is the file name Jon records it under, in media/ on the brain. A clip with no file yet is skipped and the words show as captions instead.

bulletin1.about: Act 2, lights out, on the Parlour TV: video once the files are in and the box The bulletins are videos is ticked on the Game night page; until then the brain plays the recordings and the TV shows the words. Susan reads the opening and sign-off as Ava Waves. Always clarity level 3: the opening, one family line (a wrong family, crossed off for everyone), the sign-off.

opening.text: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and all the dogs at sea! This is W-O-O-F News. We interrupt this program for a special bulletin from Sirwin Manor. At Sir Irwin's birthday party tonight, someone has been... Murderwined!

food.text: Our man on the scene reports the kitchen is clean as a whistle. Whatever happened tonight, it had nothing to do with the pie, the snacks, or anybody's chewing.

bathroom.text: Meanwhile, detectives have inspected the powder room. The roll is full, the seat is down, the air is fresh, and nobody's so much as sneezed. Nothing to see there, folks.

screens.text: In the world of technology, every gadget in the manor is behaving itself. Not a peep too loud, every charger where it belongs, no progress deleted, no message left on read, and not a single reply-all. Nothing on the airwaves tonight.

out.text: Out on the roads, traffic is moving nicely. Everybody stayed in their lane, every door was held open, and every shopping cart made it home to the corral.

slights.text: And in society news, manners at the manor are impeccable. No anniversary forgotten, no top stained, no grammar corrected, and nobody's spoiled the ending.

signoff.text: Don't touch that dial! Stay tuned for more updates.

bulletin2.about: Act 3, near the end of supper, audio on the HomePods (one AirPlay group from the brain, the Orangerie's included) with captions on the iPad. Susan reads it as Ava Waves. Jon arms it; it plays 3 to 5 minutes later. The opening, the real family's line at the clarity dial's level (1 very obscure, 5 plain), the sign-off.

opening.text: This is W-O-O-F, the Voice of Sirwin Manor! Ladies and gentlemen, pardon the interruption. Finish that bite, but listen closely. Our reporters on the scene have fresh information about tonight's Murderwined.

food.text: Reports say tempers at the manor have been simmering all evening.
Sources say somebody bit off more than they could chew.
Police say tonight's trouble has a distinct flavor to it.
Detectives are certain: somebody's stomach got the better of them.
It's official, folks: this whole mess was about food, and somebody's going to have to eat their words.

bathroom.text: Reports say something at the manor tonight just doesn't smell right.
Sources say somebody left a real mess behind them.
Police expect to flush out the culprit before the night is through.
Detectives are certain: it all happened behind the powder room door.
It's official, folks: this whole mess went down in the bathroom.

screens.text: Reports say there's been a lot of static at the manor tonight.
Sources say somebody's been pushing all the wrong buttons.
Police say tonight's trouble has everyone's wires crossed.
Detectives are certain: the trouble started on somebody's screen.
It's official, folks: this whole mess was about screens, and somebody needs to log off.

out.text: Reports say folks at the manor have been going in circles all evening.
Sources say somebody took a wrong turn somewhere tonight.
Police say this story hit a bump in the road before it got here.
Detectives are certain: it all started while somebody was out running errands.
It's official, folks: this whole mess started out in public, and somebody's got some explaining to do.

slights.text: Reports say somebody at the manor has been feeling a little self-conscious this evening.
Sources say somebody's been wishing they could disappear all night.
Police say somebody tonight was made to look a fool.
Detectives are certain: somebody was left red-faced, and they haven't gotten over it.
It's official, folks: this whole mess was about embarrassment, and somebody will never live it down.

signoff.text: That's the latest from W-O-O-F. Later this evening, Sir Irwin himself will deliver a special pup-lic address. Don't touch that dial!

closing.about: Act 7, the reveal: the closing bulletin that bookends bulletin 1, video on the Parlour TV once the files are in and the box is ticked, otherwise the recordings with the words on screen. Susan as Ava Waves opens and closes in the studio; Jon as Mic Cameron reads the four field parts. The lines are generic; the game cuts in the Murderer, Motive and Ghost cards between them. Order: Murderer, Motive, Victim. Each part's holdMs is how long its recording runs, in milliseconds: the TV shows a name card once the parts before it have had their time (finale.js). Claude Code sets them once the recordings exist.

parts.text: Good evening. This is W-O-O-F News, and we interrupt this party with breaking news. We go live now to Sirwin Manor. Mic?
Thanks, Ava. I'm standing outside Sirwin Manor, where authorities are asking everyone to be on the lookout for this character...
Police say it all started over...
...and it ended in the murder of...
Please be careful out there. The suspect may still be holding cake. Back to you in the studio.

Well, there you have it, folks. A real cat-astrophe, but this case is finally closed. Most importantly, a very happy birthday to Sir Irwin, the goodest boy in the county. And thank you to everyone who helped crack this paw-ful crime. Good night, and stay paw-sitive.
